To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the three optimisations, when implemented together, can reduce the time taken for the pipelined wave-front algorithm by up to a factor of 4.3.

(1) the OpenMP optimisation can provide up to a 3-fold increase in performance; (2) the novel restructuring of the wavefront code provides up to a 2-fold increase in performance and (3) the use of multiple sweeps through the grid can provide up to 3-fold increase performance.

(1) OpenMP parallelisation of computation blocks in the wavefront algorithm can provide a significant improvement in the overall performance; (2) the novel restructuring/shifting technique can provide a significant performance improvement, and (3) performing multiple sweeps through the wavefront data grid can also provide a significant performance gain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a predictive analytic model, which is then used to investigate the potential benefits of three optimisations to pipelined wave-front computations.
the development and application of a performance modelling methodology that is capable of evaluating the performance of optimised pipelined wave-front algorithms.
the optimisation of pipelinewavefront computations, which are ubiquitous in many applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of all three optimisations results in a performance improvement of approximately 2.4x over the original pipelined wave front algorithm.
, for the benchmark under study, the optimisations are not beneficial, and in some instances, detrimental, to performance.
, in the context of a pipelined wave-front algorithm, the optimisation techniques presented in this paper can deliver a performance increase of up to a factor of 2x.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of predictive analysis is a powerful tool in the optimisation process.

, in general, we find that: (1) the use of OpenMP to parallelise the computation of the wavefront benchmark is a viable option, although the performance gains are limited to the number of OpenMP threads used; (2) the novel shifting of computation within the benchmark is a viable optimisation, but only if the data size is sufficiently large; and (3) performing multiple sweeps through the grid is a useful optimisation, but the performance gains are dependent upon the data size.

(1) the OpenMP parallelisation of the pipelined wave front algorithm is beneficial; (2) the novel restructuring and shifting of the wavefront code is beneficial and (3) performing multiple simultaneous sweeps through the wavefront data is also beneficial.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of the three optimisations results in an average speed-up of 3.3X over the baseline pipelined wavefont implementation.
predictive analytic models, such as the one used here, can help to guide and inform the design of parallel algorithms and optimisations.

, by combining the use of the predictive model with the wavefront benchmark, it is possible to identify and quantify the performance benefits of optimisations that would not otherwise have been considered.
